body:
## Paper-side line counts per dimension: Lagrangian bound v ≤ T(2^k′+1) with exact ladder D4/D6/E7/E8 and no-gos scoped to windows h ≤ 13 (no κ claim)

Package `research/line-system-saturation`. Model, dense pairing and the polar law for odd-or-zero units are those of #446/#595/#1590 and of #2228 (Theorem 3); the T² threshold and first realisability numerics are #2125's; the 8/7 block-rank rule is #968's. This PR is **paper-side only**: how many lines a unit can carry per dimension T given the F2 rank 2k′ of its non-orthogonality adjacency. Compensation is not modelled.

**Polar law for every line system (PROVEN).** For any real line system, with labels taken from the F2 factorisation of the non-orthogonality adjacency Ā, J + Ā is admissible and equals the Gram matrix of u_t = (1, ℓ_t) under 1 ⊕ b; its rank is 2k′ + 1, or 2k′ when all labels avoid a hyperplane w^⊥. Odd-or-zero is the case Ā ≡ G mod 2 (**CHECKED** on D4, D5, D6, E6, E7, E8).

**Lagrangian saturation bound (PROVEN).** v ≤ T(2^{k′}+1), and v ≤ T·2^{k′} on the even window, with equality iff (no line orthogonal to all others, i.e. no label 0) every generator class of the symplectic polar space is a full orthogonal basis (a tight frame). The same bound holds for non-Gram units M = PQᵀ of rank T, overcomplete ones included, and the best v/T is a weighted idempotent packing number of W(2k′−1,2). **CHECKED, exact:** D4, D6, E7 attain it (3, 5, 9 lines per dimension), E8 attains 15/17 (2295 generators: 2025 full, 270 empty). A **descent** theorem (a saturated W(2k′−1,2) system yields a saturated W(2k′−3,2) system in dimension T − m_p; E7 → D6 → D4 and E8 → E7 CHECKED) shows that saturation at any k′ ≥ 4 forces a saturated k′ = 4 system. **The Schrijver-ϑ′-type two-point program P2 (and every strengthening satisfied by its symmetric optimum, including the generator inequalities) has value exactly 2^{k′}+1 for Gram units** (proof by symmetry reduction; the symmetric point is CHECKED for k′ = 2..5).

**Bounded classes (PROVEN).** Unions of unbiased frames have dense x = 1, and every admissible pairing has window ≥ F (so Kerdock/MUB-type constructions cannot beat the P104 break-even; consistent with, and not contradicting, #895's 72-clique for the full BW16 shell); norm-2 systems with products in {0, ±1} have v/T ≤ max(15, 2k′+1); symmetric multiplicity-one realisations need T ≥ d_proj(S) (Sp(10,2): 155, **PROVEN mod cite [verify]** for the group constant d_proj); uniform-angle saturated systems need λ² = 2^{k′−1}m to be a perfect square (m = 1: k′ odd). The 14 saved construction records are re-verified in exact integer arithmetic (best saturation at window h ≤ 13: 15/17 at k′ = 4, .386 at k′ = 5, .196 at k′ = 6), and the D16⁺ roots-plus-spinor family is capped at 240 + 317 = 557 lines by an exact rational Delsarte dual certificate.

**Scope and caveats.** All "cannot reach" statements are for the dense pairing, bounded windows h ≤ 13, and the repo's recorded break-even fit x\*(h) (RECORDED, not reproduced). **#2222's complete cubic-kernel unit (h ≤ 49, dense x ≈ .037, numbers RECORDED from its PR) escapes them**; no unconditional paper-side no-go exists, and it is credited as the reason for the scoping. EXPLORATORY realisability numerics are in README §10 and are not part of any claim. Tiep–Zalesskii minimal degrees, Roberson's α_p ≤ ϑ′ and Thas' ovoid theorem are cited and marked [verify]. No κ claim, no window closed, no supplier changed.

**Open next questions (README §11).** A ±1 signing of the 510-vertex doubled W(7,2) graph with S² = 60S + 256I (its non-existence would rule out a uniform-angle saturated system with one line per label at k′ = 5); level-2/three-point bounds on W(7,2); realisability of any saturated W4 system; non-dense pairings; symmetric systems of multiplicity ≥ 2.

**Verify.** `bash research/line-system-saturation/verify.sh /fresh/dir` (Python standard library only, single process, no SAT; step 0 checks `MANIFEST.sha256` and `SOURCES.json` and stops hard on mismatch; 88 PASS lines including step 0).
